prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots put B041 first, but I do not rest the case on that agreement. On the merits, GLP-1 physiology is a rare complete arc in medicine. It runs from the identification and characterisation of the active peptide, through the physiology of its insulinotropic, gut and satiety actions, to a drug class with large randomised outcome evidence in type 2 diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The discovery is original because it defined a hormone axis, not only a compound. It has been confirmed independently over decades and the clinical footprint is at its peak, so the timing is right. A citation worded around the physiology fits the Medicine prize and the three-person limit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The credited list has four names and only three places, and the drug that patients receive owes its long-acting design to Knudsen's work, which a physiology-centred citation leaves out. Priority for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is contested, and contributors outside the supplied list, such as Habener, have claims. If the committee judges that the prize must honour the drug-design step, the three-name allocation is weaker than it looks, and a configuration split between physiology and translation may be fairer. I also cannot verify the historical priority record from the files I am allowed to read.

responses.point: Sandberg backs Drucker, Holst and Mojsov and treats Knudsen's development of long-acting analogues as translational work that sits outside the three-person limit.
responses.response: I agree on the allocation but not fully on the reasoning. Calling Knudsen's work merely translational understates it, because the drugs that changed care are her designs and the Medicine prize has honoured decisive therapeutic development before. I would defend the physiology trio as the cleaner discovery citation, not because drug design is less important. I would want the committee to admit that this choice leaves a real gap, and I would not dismiss the gap by labelling it industrial.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks CAR-T second but credits only June and Sadelain, judging that Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer work is important but not CAR-specific.
responses.response: I find this a fair and useful narrowing. I put Rosenberg in my own trio, but the CAR-specific discovery is June's and Sadelain's, and Rosenberg's contribution is a broader lineage of adoptive cell therapy. A two-name B030 citation would be tighter and would also leave a place free if the committee wanted a second achievement. This is the main reason I keep B030 as my first alternative, though I still think B041 is ahead on originality and breadth of impact.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks the unfolded protein response third and the BCL-2 work fourth, and values clean attribution and mechanistic clarity alongside clinical benefit.
responses.response: I share the weight he gives to a clean two-person allocation, which makes Walter and Mori attractive. I ranked B035 fifth because its link to medicine is still indirect, as Linnarsson also notes, and the PERK arm and Ron's role are outside the credited names. I disagree that its mechanistic clarity should lift it above optogenetics or CAR-T, which show a more direct effect on the biology and practice of medicine. On BCL-2, the venetoclax translation is persuasive, but the 2002 apoptosis prize lowers the novelty and I would not move it into the preferred configuration.

responses.point: El Manira ranks optogenetics second, as a transformative circuit-analysis tool, while noting that crowded credit and its status as a tool may weaken the fit with a discovery prize.
responses.response: I agree that the method is transformative and well confirmed, and my own ranking puts it second. I weigh his point about a tool differently. The Nobel tradition has honoured methods when they opened new biology, so the tool framing is not disqualifying. The harder problem is that six credited names compete for three places, and any trio omits Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenboeck. Because the credit is so crowded, I keep it as an alternative and not the preferred prize.

uncertainties: Whether the prize should include Knudsen for drug design in place of one of the physiology names, or whether the drug-development step belongs in a separate part.
Priority for the identification of the active GLP-1 peptide and the roles of contributors outside the credited list, which I cannot verify from the provided files.
For CAR-T, whether the credit should centre on June and Sadelain alone and how to treat the originators of the chimeric receptor concept who are not credited.
Whether a two-part prize would better reflect the strength of B041 and B030 or whether a single achievement is cleaner.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile for B041, B030 or B039. I note that my field is rheumatology and autoimmunity, so B026 (TNF blockade) and B031 (cGAS-STING) are close to my expertise. I have not made either part of my preferred configuration. I will recuse if any candidate turns out to involve a documented co-author or close institutional tie.
